A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViTSP framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 33 TSPLIB instances, runtime comparisons, and selector ablations, including supplementary plots.

after.justification: v2 reports original TSPLIB evaluations and adds synthetic TSP-10K results, initialization ablations, and measurements of selection effectiveness and API costs.

M1.justification: Section 3, the prompts, and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same initialization, visual selection, zooming, subproblem reformulation, solver acceptance, and asynchronous orchestration procedures. Testing FI initialization is an ablation of the existing framework.

E1.justification: v2 retains all 33 TSPLIB instances and adds evaluation on 16 uniformly distributed synthetic instances with 10,000 nodes. Table 3 extends the previously real-world-only evaluation to a controlled synthetic distribution, while retaining the TSP task.

E2.justification: SIT is added as an evaluated comparator across the retained TSPLIB benchmark in Tables 1–2. The earlier comparator set remains present; changes to DeepACO settings are protocol changes.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a 600-second synthetic benchmark budget, matched-runtime initialization controls, and selection-validity and API-cost measurements. Appendix F.3 also changes the stated DeepACO ant count from 500 to 100; unchanged TSPLIB scores do not establish whether that experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained random-selector ablations, Table 4 adds a systematic LKH-versus-FI initialization study across TSPLIB. Appendix I adds quantitative analyses of successful subproblem selections and API costs, substantially expanding evidence about component dependence and practical efficiency.

E5.justification: v2 first explicitly reports averaging ViTSP gaps and runtimes over five runs, also using five-run averages for initialization, validity, and cost analyses. v1 does not specify comparable repeated-run aggregation. No dispersion estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: TSPLIB gaps and runtimes are extensively revised alongside newly stated five-run averaging: the reported overall ViTSP gap changes from 0.19% to 0.24%, and pla85900 from 0.65% to 0.83%. New SIT, initialization, validity, and cost results appear. Synthetic Table 3 reports gaps of 0.70% for ViTSP and 1.06% for LKH-3. These are revised or newly reported estimates, not established same-protocol performance changes.

T1.justification: The TSP definitions, objective, asymmetric-to-symmetric reformulation, distance matrices, and solution recovery remain mathematically unchanged. Neither version adds formal theoretical guarantees or proofs beyond the retained formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract revises the claimed average gap from below 0.2% to 0.24% and the reduction relative to LKH-3 from 12–100% to 3.57–100%. The central training-free, scalable hybrid-framework contribution remains unchanged. The introduction still retains the earlier reduction range.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of initialization dependence and multimodal prompting, plus limitations concerning selector–solver coordination, large-versus-small subproblem tradeoffs, and batch throughput. The earlier dense-region and joint-neighborhood explanations remain in Appendix H.

D1.justification: v2 discloses per-instance LKH RUNS values in Table 5, a consistent 20-by-20 figure size, SIT checkpoint and refinement details, and additional DeepACO parameters. It explicitly clarifies inclusion of API latency in runtime and replaces the listed anonymous code location with a named Purdue repository.

R1.justification: Luo et al. (2025), supporting the added SIT comparison, is newly cited. The main related-work narrative and positioning remain largely unchanged. Updated years for Fast T2T and UDC refer to the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction and results rewrites, adds 'Solving' to the title, and introduces ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. New appendix sections organize the added analyses, while the existing method and related-work structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The original 33-instance table is split into Tables 1–2, and five additional tables display benchmarks, ablations, settings, validity rates, and costs. Appendix plot panels are reordered, Figure 6 is relocated with an expanded caption, and conference formatting substantially changes the title block, headers, and page composition.

improvement.justification: The synthetic comparison, initialization ablation, and iteration/cost analyses improve assessment of generality, dependence on warm starts, and practical expense. Explicit averaging and implementation details improve transparency. These gains are tempered by absent run-to-run uncertainty and unreconciled prose: the introduction retains the old reduction range, and the scalability discussion excludes SIT despite its successful pla85900 result in Table 2.
